descriptions.adipose: Large, unilocular adipocytes are arranged in a classic honeycomb or chicken-wire architecture with minimal intervening stroma. The intracellular spaces appear optically clear and unstained due to lipid dissolution during tissue processing, separated by very thin, delicate eosinophilic cell borders creating an open, web-like texture. Nuclei are small, hyperchromatic, and distinctly flattened or crescent-shaped, pushed peripherally and compressed tightly against the outer plasma membrane.
descriptions.background: This non-tissue background region is characterized by a complete absence of intact cellular architecture, stromal framework, or identifiable basophilic nuclei. The field displays a predominantly smooth, empty, and bright white to pale translucent appearance devoid of organized tissue patterning. Staining is virtually non-existent, lacking characteristic purple hematoxylin and pink eosin uptake, and is limited to clear glass slide area with occasional faint illumination gradients, out-of-focus blur, or sparse amorphous non-cellular debris.
descriptions.debris: Debris displays a complete loss of organized tissue architecture, presenting as an unorganized, heterogeneous mixture of necrotic material, mucus, luminal remnants, and lysed cellular breakdown products. Intact cells and structured nuclei are largely absent, replaced by hyperchromatic, pyknotic, or fragmented basophilic nuclear dust and karyorrhectic debris with indistinct cell borders. The background exhibits a smudgy, flocculent, or coarsely granular texture characterized by variable eosinophilic to amphophilic proteinaceous staining, often interspersed with irregular, pale or empty optical clearings.
descriptions.lymphocytes: Small, round to ovoid mononuclear cells characterized by an exceptionally high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio with an imperceptible or scant rim of pale cytoplasm. The nuclei are intensely hyperchromatic and deeply basophilic on H&E staining, exhibiting dense, coarse, clumped chromatin without prominent nucleoli. They typically appear as diffuse interstitial infiltrates scattered throughout the stroma or assembled into dense, sheet-like lymphoid aggregates.
descriptions.mucus: Expansive extracellular pools or lakes of pale basophilic, light blue-gray, or faintly amphophilic amorphous material dominate the field, dissecting through the background tissue architecture. The mucinous matrix exhibits a delicate, wispy, or fibrillar texture, often appearing glassy and largely acellular to hypocellular. Suspended within the mucin are sparse detached degenerate epithelial fragments, rare inflammatory cells, or occasional signet ring-like cells featuring compressed, crescentic, and eccentrically displaced nuclei.
descriptions.smooth_muscle: Smooth muscle tissue is composed of compact, intersecting or parallel fascicles of elongated, spindle-shaped cells with abundant, fibrillar eosinophilic cytoplasm. The nuclei are centrally located, monomorphic, and classically cigar-shaped with rounded, blunt ends and finely dispersed chromatin. Depending on the plane of section, the tissue exhibits a streaming, wavy architecture in longitudinal cuts or a regular mosaic of polygonal cells with central round nuclei in cross-section.
descriptions.normal_colon_mucosa: Normal colonic mucosa displays an orderly architecture of parallel, test-tube-shaped tubular crypts or uniform circular cross-sectional lumens lined by a simple columnar epithelium rich in clear, rounded goblet cells. The epithelial nuclei are monomorphic, oval, and strictly polarized at the basal aspect with smooth contours, fine chromatin texture, and an absence of stratification or marked atypia. Hematoxylin and eosin staining demonstrates a striking contrast between pale, translucent apical cytoplasmic mucin vacuoles and deeply basophilic basal nuclei, all supported by a delicate, moderately cellular lamina propria.
descriptions.cancer_associated_stroma: Cancer-associated stroma is characterized by a reactive desmoplastic proliferation of spindle-shaped to plump fibroblasts and myofibroblasts arranged in streaming fascicles, intersecting bands, or loose haphazard arrays. These stromal cells possess elongated, tapered, or vesicular basophilic nuclei embedded within an abundant fibrillar and collagen-rich extracellular matrix. The tissue displays a distinctive eosinophilic, fibrous texture that varies from dense pink collagenous bundles to pale, amphophilic myxoid areas, occasionally interspersed with small, darkly staining infiltrating lymphocytes.
descriptions.colorectal_adenocarcinoma: Infiltrative, crowded, and irregularly branched or cribriform malignant glandular structures are arranged within a pale desmoplastic stroma, frequently enclosing luminal eosinophilic necrotic debris. The neoplastic columnar-to-cuboidal epithelial cells exhibit loss of basal polarity, pseudostratification, and variable amounts of amphophilic to eosinophilic cytoplasm. Nuclei are markedly enlarged, pleomorphic, and hyperchromatic with irregular membranes, coarse clumped chromatin, and prominent nucleoli, resulting in dense basophilic clusters with frequent atypical mitotic figures.

prompt_template: You are a pathologist writing a detailed morphological description for the class {class_name!r} (dataset: {dataset}), to be encoded by a vision-language model's text tower and compared against histopathology image patches. Cover: cell/nuclear shape, arrangement or architecture, texture, and any distinctive staining pattern. 2-4 sentences. Output only the description, no preamble, no quotes.
